scope: Read-only repository and existing-data audit; no model implementation or training.

baseline.validation_selection: mean of participant-macro SBP and DBP MAE

clinical_mapping.result: All observed CaseIDs map to the numeric SubjectID stored locally
clinical_mapping.note: Response is gzip-compressed UTF-8 with BOM; timestamps anonymized to casestart=0.

candidate_personalization_cohort.status: availability-based proposal; task and final protocol require confirmation
candidate_personalization_cohort.allocation_algorithm: Sort eligible SubjectIDs lexicographically, NumPy default_rng(20261009).shuffle; first six targets, next four development.

limitations: No actual cuff/NIBP events in either existing data representation.
Official subset row order cannot define chronological forecasting.
Do not use Subject source suffix _1 as visit ID.
p005878 contains two cases with resetting timestamps; separate record grouping required.
Absolute inter-session dates absent; age suggests case order but does not establish visit interval.
Upstream raw-to-125Hz resampling support is undocumented in distributed code; original-device-time causal guarantees remain unverified.
Reference-dependent PulseDB quality selection is already applied and cannot be undone from retained segments.
The existing pretrained checkpoint contains several proposed personalization subjects and cannot be used as a clean population initializer.

final_personalization_protocol.task: Early personal ECG/PPG and scalar ABP-derived reference calibration, followed by contemporaneous SBP/DBP estimation from later observed ECG/PPG
final_personalization_protocol.calibration_interpretation: Simulation using sparse invasive-ABP-derived scalar references; 60-second spacing does not establish independent cuff measurement events.
final_personalization_protocol.candidate_history: candidate_personalization_cohort preserves the original availability-based proposal unchanged.

replacement.reason: Only six 60-second-spaced support windows in first 20% of elapsed retained-record span; required ten.
replacement.selection_rule: Next unused subject in original seeded eligible permutation; development assignments unchanged; no model performance inspected.

final_personalization_protocol.calibration_period: b = first_sample + 0.20 * (last_sample + 1/125 - first_sample), using elapsed time and within one record.
final_personalization_protocol.support_eligibility: Window end-exclusive <= b; greedy chronological pool with window starts at least 60 seconds apart.
final_personalization_protocol.support_selection: From greedy pool, select np.rint(np.linspace(0, len(pool)-1, 10)).astype(int); NumPy ties-to-even rounding. Budgets use chronological prefixes of the selected ten windows.
final_personalization_protocol.query_selection: Window first_sample >= b + 10 seconds. Query rows are identical for every strategy and budget within a patient.
final_personalization_protocol.adaptation_application_time: b, common to all budgets; actual final-reference times and their ages are recorded separately.
final_personalization_protocol.time_units: Seconds relative to each PulseDB retrieved recording clip; no absolute wall-clock dates.
final_personalization_protocol.interval_convention: [first_sample_s,end_exclusive_s); exactly 1250 samples at 125 Hz. The last stored sample is end_exclusive_s - 0.008.
final_personalization_protocol.source_index_convention: Zero-based column index into Subj_Wins fields; arrays inside each patient record inherit patient_id, subject_id, case_id, and source_file from their parent.
final_personalization_protocol.duration_interpretation: Retained observed-window duration is distinct from elapsed span and spaced-reference period.
